goal: On the Requests surface, let an owner review a built batch's rendered Outreach rows, approve it (approval_method='owner', CAS'd on approved_at IS NULL, veto_deadline_at = approved_at + 15 minutes), exclude individual Asks, and stop it through the Halt latch.
non_goals: Owner edit of a rendered ask (D22 — approve or exclude only)
Per-ask regenerate affordance (route + budget UI) — deferred to its own map #617 ticket
Admin/support halt surface — admin_halt stays a CHECK member with no writer
Any dispatch, release or send — the releaser and send worker are #630; this feature ships inert
Auto-approval (auto_policy) lane, Judge availability, trust dial — #631
Notification or FYI email on owner approval — the owner just acted
New analytics event names (would require a migration for ci:analytics-events)
user_visible_behavior: With SOLICITATION_SEND_ENABLED on, a built batch shows an approval panel above the funnel hero listing every rendered Outreach row (subject + body) with a per-ask exclude control
A moderation_high attempt appears as a count and reason only — never its subject or body (D6a)
The approve control is present only when every send Ask has a non-cancelled Outreach row; until then the panel says the batch is still being prepared
Approving records the approval, cancels every excluded ask, and moves the batch into its 15-minute veto window
During the veto window and after sending starts, the owner sees a single stop control; using it halts the batch permanently and says so
A batch past its 7-day approval window shows an expired state with no approve control
A halted or closed batch is read-only and states that it cannot be resumed
With SOLICITATION_SEND_ENABLED off, the Requests screen is byte-identical to watch-mode today
invariants: Invariant #3 by analogy (spec §9A): no email may leave without approval_method recorded on the batch; this feature records approval_method='owner' only
Invariant #4 ported: a moderation_high rendered body is never owner-readable, at the read model and at RLS
Invariant #8: every approval and halt read/write is scoped by account_id AND business_id
Invariant #11: entitlement gated on subscriptionGrantsFullAccess, never a raw === 'active'
Invariant #13: SOLICITATION_SEND_ENABLED is server-authoritative; no NEXT_PUBLIC companion
Invariant #15: every src/lib module takes sql/tx as an explicit parameter
The Halt latch is monotone — halted_at, halt_reason and halted_by never change once written, and there is no resume
Approval is idempotent — approved_at, approval_method, approved_by_user_id and veto_deadline_at are CAS'd on approved_at IS NULL, so a double-submit re-approves nothing
What was approved is byte-for-byte what sends — approval is refused while any send Ask lacks an Outreach row, so no row can render after approval and become releasable unseen
Lock order is batch → run (spec amendment B11): the approval and halt transactions take acquireSolicitationBatchLock before any run-spine write
Parent terminalization has exactly one owner — closeBatchIfSettled — and the approval and halt transactions call it rather than terminalizing directly
edge_cases: Owner excludes every ask and approves: allowed; the approval transaction cancels all rows owner_excluded and calls closeBatchIfSettled, which settles the batch exhausted and terminalizes the send parent completed
Approval attempted while generation is still rendering: refused with a distinct 409 the UI renders as 'still preparing', re-validated inside the transaction under the batch lock
Approval attempted on a batch past built_at + 7 days: refused; the batch is expired and neither lane may approve it
Double-submit of approve: second write is a no-op, response reports already-approved rather than an error
Halt during the veto window records owner_veto; halt after sending_started_at records owner_halt — the reason is derived server-side from batch state, never sent by the client
Halt cancels Outreach rows in rendered and queued and deliberately never a row in sending
Second halt is a no-op; halt of an already-closed batch is refused
Halt of a batch that was never approved is allowed (it is the owner discarding a built batch) and records owner_halt
A batch whose asks were all withheld at generation has no rendered rows: the panel shows the spoilage report and no approve control
Partially-generated batch after generation exhaustion: holes are already withheld/render_failed rows, so the settled predicate is satisfied and approval proceeds over what rendered
Cross-account or cross-location batch id: uniform 404, same exposure as an unknown row
past_due account inside its 7-day grace still approves; cancelled or pending_payment does not
trialing is treated as full access
Location switch mid-flight: an approval response for a superseded scope is never rendered against the newly selected location

rollback_plan: Migration 108 is a single CHECK widening on solicitation_outreach (adds 'owner_excluded' to the cancel disposition set) with no data change; roll back by re-applying 091's constraint text verbatim, which is safe because no row can carry the new value until this feature ships. The whole surface is behind SOLICITATION_SEND_ENABLED, which is unset (off) in every environment including staging, so a revert of the code needs no flag flip. Revert order: revert the merge commit, then re-apply the 091 constraint on staging first and prod second, in lockstep.
observability: Structured log 'batch_approved' from the approve route: businessId, batchId, approvedCount, excludedCount, alreadyApproved — no rendered subject or body ever interpolated
Structured log 'batch_halted' from the halt route: businessId, batchId, haltReason, cancelledCount, alreadyHalted
Run steps 'batch_approved' and 'batch_halted' on the solicitation_send_batch parent (append-only, actor and counts in detail) — the immutable record D9 requires; step keys are TS-only so no migration

How I would know it broke: an approved batch with approval_method IS NULL, or a halted batch with outreach rows still in rendered/queued, or a batch_approved log line whose approvedCount disagrees with the outreach rows left live
